_comment: Kind-library test artifacts (protocol step 4, authored BEFORE mapper code — slice 2 entry obligation). Three families per the ratified Test_Artifacts sheet: construct (one smallest file per kind, empty remainder), adversarial (the corpse catalog — where PM-4's clean-room bet is secured), remainder (each deferred construct -> exactly that counted remainder). Every case: sql + expected assertions the mapper test walks.

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A <> 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A != 1
construct._witness: two syntaxes, ONE kind — syntax lives in evidence

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A > 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A >= 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A < 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A <= 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A !< 1
construct._witness: legacy synonym normalizes to the meaning

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A !> 1
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A LIKE 'X%'
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IN (1, 2, 3)
construct._witness: members are one comparand edge each, ordered by position

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IN (SELECT B FROM dbo.U)
construct._witness: structural split: the comparand is a subquery_ref, never string-matched

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A BETWEEN 1 AND 9
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IS NULL
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.U)
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A > ALL (SELECT B FROM dbo.U)
construct._witness: RG-1 ruling: operator + quantifier are node PROPERTIES, not roles; property values are ScriptDom's own enum names — dialect-labeled evidence

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1 AND B = 2
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1 OR B = 2
construct._witness: an OR is a NODE — no walk can silently read it as AND

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A NOT LIKE 'X%'
construct._witness: R1: ALL negated syntax normalizes to structural NOT over the positive kind

construct.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A NOT IN (1, 2)
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IS NOT NULL
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 9
SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE (A = 1)
construct._witness: parentheses shape the tree, then dissolve — the structure IS the grouping

adversarial.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1 OR B = 2 AND C = 3
adversarial._witness: corpse: AND binds tighter; a flat walk would misread membership

adversarial.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE (A = 1 OR B = 2) AND C = 3
adversarial._witness: corpse: same predicates, different tree — the parens dissolve but their SHAPE stays

adversarial.sql: SELECT X.A FROM (SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1) X WHERE X.A > 5
adversarial._witness: CHECK-KG2-4: the inner predicate is owned by the inner scope, never hoisted

adversarial.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A BETWEEN B AND C
adversarial._witness: corpse: bounds need not be literals

adversarial.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IN (SELECT CODE FROM dbo.VALUE_SET WHERE SET_ID = 7)
adversarial._witness: the clinical value-set pattern: the decision's content lives in DATA

adversarial.sql: WITH Base AS (SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A = 1) SELECT B.A FROM Base B
adversarial._witness: the staging chain as graph structure — Base resolves within the tree

remainder.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE A IS DISTINCT FROM 1
remainder._witness: R2 deferred: SQL 2022 null-safe equality; counted, revisit on first estate sighting. CAUGHT AT BUILD: ScriptDom emits DistinctPredicate, not the draft registry's BooleanIsDistinctFromExpression

remainder.sql: SELECT A FROM dbo.T WHERE CONTAINS(A, 'x')
remainder._witness: R3 deferred: full-text predicate; counted, never guessed
